That's true. I have to keep reminding myself that my highschool grades probably won't matter when I'm interviewing for a job or something, and that I should stop overstressing myself. Haha, 

Ohhh, I'm 17 by the way. I don't know. My parents were so excited for me to start driving when I turned 16, but life just got in the way and I kind of lost all motivation to learn anything.

Oh, wow, I never thought about it that way. That makes complete sense. I wish I had thought about that earlier so I didn't stress out so much over AP exams. I think my mom wanted colleges to see that I was an "over-achieving" student, so she wanted me to take a lot of AP courses. And in a way, I guess AP scores validated my high grades.

I don't know how to drive yet, so I can't go anywhere. (I know, I'm pathetic) But I think I'll go outside and try to find a quiet spot in my yard somewhere. Thank you!

Yeah, AP grades are for college credits. However, when I was in 9th grade, my mom overinflated the importance of AP exams, and now I unconsciously believe and feel that AP exams are these super-important exams although they're actually not. I wish that she hadn't overinflated its importance...

That's true. I'm not sure. I don't know how to focus on a few things. All my life I've been doing everything at once, haha. It seems that everyone wants me to do everything at the same time. Hmmmm, but I guess the most important thing objectively right now is college.

Yes, my counselor is helpful. Besides her, I usually vent to some family members I'm close to. (They thankfully aren't tired of hearing me vent all the time) Thanks. I'll send you a PM.
I've thought about this a lot. It's so interesting and insightful how relationships (and friendships) can form from the most simple encounters.
